svg.aria-label: Architecture of the guideline formalization system. Four stages run left to right: extract, ground, formalize, and check. Each stage contains deterministic components plus a small number of model calls whose output space is constrained. Each stage terminates in an explicit output — a statement with its source span, then the closed vocabulary, then a validated rule — and an arrow carries that output into the first component of the next stage. A residue channel runs beneath all four stages, carrying six refusal reasons. One is set deterministically by the binder and one by the validator; a third is mixed; the remaining three require a model.

text.tspan: Parses JATS, HTML or PDF into one Block type.
Recommendation callouts and tables come already
tagged by the publisher, so recall is structural
rather than a matter of wording. Text is cleaned
for matching; every offset maps back to the raw.
Scores every candidate on grading vocabulary,
deontic phrasing and section context. Below
threshold, no model is ever called on it — which
is what keeps a 600-candidate document affordable.
Decides two things per candidate: does this direct
clinical action, and is it about a patient rather
than a service. The answer must include a quote
from the source, checked as a verbatim substring;
a paraphrase is rejected and the heuristic runs.

svg.text: verbatim, with a locator and character offsets

text.tspan: Pulls the clinical concepts out of a sentence as
exact substrings, each tagged as a lab, condition,
drug, drug class or procedure — the tag decides
which terminologies are searched at all.
One mention becomes several queries: the abbreviation
resolved through the document's own glossary,
compounds split, head noun alone. Candidates are
ranked by word overlap over SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm,
ATC and VSAC, then by MEANING for the pairs that
share no words — kidney function against Renal
function. A candidate counts as evidence only on an
exact term, matching units, or full token coverage.

svg.text: it returns a position in the list above,
so a code is not a thing it can say
a choice outside the range is rejected, and
so is a boolean: True would pass as index 1
deterministic fallback — also the offline path
abstains on a near-tie, a unit mismatch, or
a best match with no positive evidence

text.tspan: Four sources, not one: a variable per verified
binding; events for the bound concepts a date can
be measured from; a dose variable where the sentence
changes one; and, on the second pass, the declared
holes. Plausible ranges are the caller's to supply,
and none are supplied.
Re-derives the binding without the model. A code
absent from the index means a stale cache; a lab
bound to SNOMED means a mis-wired index; a missing
version means the meaning drifts silently; a lone
code where a set was needed means siblings fail.

svg.text: the closed vocabulary the decoder is confined to

text.tspan: What a rule may say: a comparison, an interval, a
recency window, a relative change from the patient's
own earlier state, and boolean structure. Which of
these the decoder was actually offered is recorded
beside a refusal, so a gap is not read as a limit.
Writes the rule, or declines to — the schema admits
exactly one of the two, and the model must commit.
Variable and event names are enumerated from the
registry, so an unknown name cannot appear; the
grammar is unrolled to a fixed depth to stay legal.
Checks the tree in pure Python: literal types against
declared ones, operators defined for those types,
intervals that contain something, a page and a
sentence to cite, an obligation over something a plan
can change, and a relative change measured from a
distinct event rather than from itself.
Merges variables that resolved to the same code, so
a rule written over two names for one concept is read
as what it truly says. Similarity judgements are never
trusted — only an identical system, code and version.
Asks Z3 whether the rule can ever apply, whether an
applicable patient can ever comply, and whether anyone
can violate it — and warns if it applies to everyone.
A rule no patient can fail certifies nothing, and
compiles perfectly while doing so.
Compares the rule back against the sentence it came
from. A number stated in the text but absent from the
rule, or a concept that bound and then went unused,
is surfaced for a reviewer rather than dropped — an
unused outcome is fine, a dropped population is not.
Encodes over bound vocabulary only, k times; how often
it declines across k becomes the confidence score.
If any concept failed to bind, a clean strict result
is NOT trusted, because the omission leaves a rule
that still typechecks. It retries with the undefined
predicate, quoted from the statement, as a variable
carrying no code, no source and no assumed range.
Reads whether the guideline requires the action or
merely offers it. A permission has no violating
patient, so it accuses no one — and GRADE-conditional
is not permission: weak evidence, not an option.

svg.text: φ = when → then, an operator, and any named holes

text.tspan: Builds one symbolic patient from the registry and
bounds each variable by its plausible range, so a
counterexample is a person a clinician will accept.
Recency becomes an occurrence flag and a day count,
because a solver has no timeline. Those ranges are
hand-curated, and none are currently set.
Emits a standalone library over FHIR. Value sets carry
the version a reviewer can resolve themselves,
thresholds keep their units, recency becomes a dated
query, and a hole is left null rather than assumed
false. Unresolved names and unclosed brackets are
caught with no compiler present and fed back for a
bounded number of retries, then it refuses. An absent
compiler warns; it never reads as a pass.
A permission gets outcomes of its own — taken, not
taken, available, not applicable. None of them is a
finding against anyone, and that is guaranteed by the
operator rather than by editing a verdict string.
Writes the machine artifact and a page for a person:
each source sentence beside the rule it became, the
guideline's own wording of its strength, the findings
raised per statement, and the refusals listed
alongside rather than in a separate document.

svg.text: DECLARED RESIDUE — published beside the rules, never dropped
MIXED — the solver, else the model

ONE of the six is deterministic evidence from the binder, and one more from this stage's validator; a third is mixed. The other three need the model — to decline, or, for not_patient_level, to have classified the statement upstream.

So the deterministic machinery is a GATE ON the model's answer, not a replacement for it. Attribution is reported separately again: an index gap or a transport failure is our bug, not the guideline's residue.
